audit.intended_rules: Ch.4 advance booking window (7-day hard rejection vs 21-day international guidance — ticket issued 20 days out is a near-threshold distractor); Ch.4 cabin class (economy mandatory for short segments); Ch.4 taxes/surcharges (all four fee lines are mandatory taxes and carrier-imposed YQ surcharge, fully reimbursable); Ch.13/Figure 1 weekend rule (Sunday return covered by named conference in note).
handbook_issues: Minor ambiguity: Ch.3 requires written pre-approval for international flights and says to state the approver in the submission note, but the note only states the trip purpose. Ch.2's canonical list of required flight-note facts does not include pre-approval and Ch.3's sanction is soft ('may be rejected'), so the case still adjudicates to full approval — but a strict reader could argue a missing approver statement. Worth a line in instructor notes if this case is kept.
audit.notes: Validator passes. Fully reimbursable: €794.80 (base fare €540 + €78.50 DE passenger service fee + €42.10 LuftSiG security charge + €38.20 Helsinki departure tax + €96.00 YQ surcharge). Issued 20 days before the first international segment: below the 21-day 'book early' guidance but above the enforced 7-day rejection window, making it a good near-threshold distractor. Economy cabin on ~3.5h/2.5h FRA-HEL segments complies. All fee lines are mandatory taxes/surcharges; no seat, lounge, Wi-Fi, or bag fees. Receipt dated Friday 2024-04-12, so Figure 1 is not triggered by the receipt date; the Sunday return is covered by the named conference (Nordic Tech Summit) in the note. Vendor details realistic (Lufthansa, 60549 Frankfurt). No label.json exists; if one is added it should be decision=approved, claimed=reimbursed=794.80, all five line items fully reimbursed, citing Ch.4 booking window, cabin class, and taxes/surcharges rules.
